scope: The American century to the AI revolution, 1945-2026: the transistor, the integrated circuit, the microprocessor, the foundry, the GPU, CUDA, AlexNet, the transformer, scaling at OpenAI, ChatGPT and the 2026 frontier, told as nine periods and sixteen moments.

facts.claim: After the Second World War the United States was responsible for half of global industrial output.
quotes: In the Post–World War II economic expansion, the US was responsible for half of global industrial output, held 80 percent of the world's gold reserves, and was the world's sole nuclear power.

facts.claim: After the Second World War the United States held 80 percent of the world's gold reserves.
quotes: In the Post–World War II economic expansion, the US was responsible for half of global industrial output, held 80 percent of the world's gold reserves, and was the world's sole nuclear power.

facts.claim: GDP in 1950 was 1,456 billion 1990 dollars in the United States, 510 in the Soviet Union and 161 in Japan.
quotes: GDP levels in 1950 (in billion 1990 dollars) were 510 (100%) in the Soviet Union, 161 (100%) in Japan and 1,456 (100%) in the United States.
facts.notes: The same fact feeds the USSR and Japan series; the 1990-dollar basis is Maddison-style purchasing-power GDP.

facts.claim: The Soviet Union had the world's second-largest economy and the largest standing military.
quotes: It had the world's second-largest economy and the largest standing military.
facts.notes: Wikipedia states it without a year; the value is the year the state ended.

facts.claim: The United States transferred US$13.3 billion to 17 European countries under the Marshall Plan.
quotes: The United States transferred US$13.3 billion to 17 European countries (equivalent to $141 billion[A] in 2025[B]) in economic recovery programs to Western European economies after the end of World War II in Europe.

facts.claim: In a Life magazine editorial of 17 February 1941 Henry Luce urged the United States to forsake isolationism for the role of the world's Good Samaritan.
quotes: In a February 17, 1941, Life magazine editorial Luce, the son of missionaries, urged the United States to forsake isolationism for a missionary's role, acting as the world's Good Samaritan and spreading democracy.

facts.claim: At Bretton Woods in 1944 the United States, which controlled two-thirds of the world's gold, insisted that the system rest on both gold and the dollar.
quotes: The United States, which controlled two-thirds of the world's gold, insisted that the Bretton Woods system rest on both gold and the US dollar.
facts.notes: Wikipedia's Pax Americana article says 80 percent of reserves; this article says two-thirds of the world's gold. The sources differ and both are recorded.

facts.claim: Eleven Nobel Prizes and five Turing Awards have been awarded for work completed at Bell Laboratories.
quotes: Eleven Nobel Prizes and five Turing Awards have been awarded for work completed at Bell Laboratories.

facts.claim: Fairchild Semiconductor was started in 1957 to make silicon transistors when germanium was still the most common semiconductor material.
quotes: In 1957, the Fairchild Semiconductor division was started with plans to make silicon transistors at a time when germanium was still the most common material for semiconductor use.

facts.claim: The eight founders of Fairchild were Julius Blank, Victor Grinich, Jean Hoerni, Eugene Kleiner, Jay Last, Gordon Moore, Robert Noyce and Sheldon Roberts.
quotes: The eight men were Julius Blank, Victor Grinich, Jean Hoerni, Eugene Kleiner, Jay Last, Gordon Moore, Robert Noyce, and Sheldon Roberts.

facts.claim: Jack Kilby took part, with Robert Noyce of Fairchild, in realizing the first integrated circuit at Texas Instruments in 1958.
quotes: Clair Kilby (November 8, 1923 – June 20, 2005) was an American electrical engineer who took part, along with Robert Noyce of Fairchild Semiconductor, in the realization of the first integrated circuit while working at Texas Instruments in 1958.

facts.claim: In 1965 Gordon Moore, then director of research and development at Fairchild Semiconductor, was asked for a ten-year prediction for the semiconductor industry.
quotes: In 1965, Gordon Moore, who at the time was working as the director of research and development at Fairchild Semiconductor, was asked to contribute to the thirty-fifth-anniversary issue of Electronics magazine with a prediction on the future of the semiconductor components industry over the next ten years.

facts.claim: In 1975 Moore revised his forecast to a doubling of components every two years, a compound annual growth rate of 41 percent.
quotes: In 1975, looking forward to the next decade, he revised the forecast to doubling every two years, a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 41%.

facts.claim: The silicon-gate process let a single Intel 4004 chip contain 2,300 transistors.
quotes: Together, these innovations doubled the circuit density, and thus halved cost, allowing a single chip to contain 2,300 transistors and run five times faster than designs using the previous MOS technology with aluminum gates.

facts.claim: Intel made the first commercial microprocessor in 1971, but it was the success of the PC in the early 1980s that made it Intel's primary business.
quotes: Although Intel created the world's first commercial microprocessor chip—the Intel 4004—in 1971, it was not until the success of the PC in the early 1980s that this became its primary business.

moments.title: The war ends, the American century begins
moments.advantage: half of world industry, 80% of the gold
moments.mechanism: The only large economy not bombed produced half of global industrial output and held most of the gold, so it wrote the monetary rules and paid for Europe's recovery.
moments.outcome: Bretton Woods put the dollar at the centre; the Marshall Plan moved US$13.3 billion to 17 countries; by 1950 US GDP was 1,456 billion 1990 dollars against the USSR's 510.

moments.title: The transistor at Bell Labs
moments.mechanism: Three Bell Labs physicists made a working solid-state amplifier, financed by a regulated telephone monopoly that could afford basic research.
moments.outcome: Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley shared the 1956 Nobel Prize; Bell Labs work has won eleven Nobel Prizes in all.

moments.title: The traitorous eight
moments.mechanism: Eight engineers walked out of Shockley's laboratory, found a backer in Sherman Fairchild, and bet on silicon when germanium was the norm.
moments.outcome: Fairchild was founded on 18 September 1957; by 1960 it was the incubator of the valley.

moments.title: The planar process and the monolithic integrated circuit
moments.mechanism: Hoerni's planar process let Noyce put every component on one flat silicon chip that could be mass-produced, where Kilby's 1958 germanium circuit had wires.
moments.outcome: Fairchild's first batch of 100 devices sold to IBM at $150 each for the B-70 bomber's computer.

moments.title: The microprocessor
moments.mechanism: Intel's silicon-gate process doubled circuit density, putting 2,300 transistors on one chip built for a Japanese calculator maker.
moments.outcome: The 4004 launched on 15 November 1971; Moore revised his law to a doubling every two years in 1975.

moments.title: The IBM PC and the x86 lock-in
moments.advantage: the instruction set every PC maker needed
moments.mechanism: The IBM PC used an Intel 8088; Compaq's 1986 80386 clone beat IBM to the next chip and made Intel the key supplier, after Japanese memory makers squeezed Intel out of DRAM in 1983.
moments.outcome: Intel became a microprocessor company: the 4004's field became its primary business only in the early 1980s.

moments.title: The pure-play foundry
moments.mechanism: A Taiwanese government-backed joint venture, funded by Philips, built chips only for others, so any designer could start a company without a fab.
moments.outcome: TSMC held 72.5% of top-10 foundry revenue in Q2 2026 and 79% of its Q3 2026 wafer revenue came from 7nm and below.

moments.title: The GeForce 256, the first GPU
moments.mechanism: After nearly dying in 1996 (staff cut from 100 to 40) Nvidia shipped on a six-month cycle and put 17 million transistors on a TSMC-made chip it marketed as the first GPU.
moments.outcome: Nvidia listed in January 1999; in December 2000 it agreed to acquire 3dfx's intellectual assets.

moments.title: CUDA opens the GPU to programmers
moments.advantage: a programming platform on every GeForce
moments.mechanism: Created in 2004 and released in 2007, CUDA let researchers write general programs for graphics chips already sitting in their machines.
moments.outcome: CUDA is now 20 years old and has 6 million developers.

moments.title: AlexNet on two GTX 580s
moments.advantage: deep learning only worked on GPUs
moments.mechanism: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton trained a 60-million-parameter network for five to six days on two $500 gaming cards, beating the runner-up by more than ten points.
moments.outcome: Top-5 error 15.3%; the field moved to GPUs and Nvidia's chips became research infrastructure.

moments.title: Attention Is All You Need
moments.advantage: an architecture that parallelises on GPUs
moments.mechanism: Eight Google researchers dropped recurrence, so training could be spread across thousands of GPUs; the advantage was published rather than kept.
moments.outcome: Cited more than 150,000 times; all eight authors later left Google.

moments.title: OpenAI scales the transformer
moments.advantage: the bet that loss falls as a power law with scale
moments.mechanism: Kaplan et al. showed loss falls as a power law in size, data and compute; OpenAI turned that into GPT-3, ten times larger than any prior dense model, on Microsoft's compute.
moments.outcome: Parameters went 117 million (2018), 1.5 billion (2019), 175 billion (2020); Microsoft licensed GPT-3 exclusively in September 2020.

moments.title: ChatGPT
moments.advantage: distribution: a product anyone could use
moments.mechanism: A chat interface on a scaled transformer reached 100 million monthly users in two months, with Microsoft adding $10 billion and Azure compute in January 2023.
moments.outcome: 900 million weekly users by February 2026; OpenAI valued at $500 billion in October 2025 and $852 billion in March 2026.

moments.title: The AI revolution reaches Nvidia
moments.advantage: every frontier lab runs on its GPUs
moments.mechanism: Demand from clouds and labs for CUDA systems took Nvidia from $1 trillion to $2 trillion in 180 days and to $5 trillion on 29 October 2025.
moments.outcome: Nvidia is valued at $4.506 trillion in November 2026, with a 75% accelerator share, down from 87% in 2024.

moments.title: DeepSeek's cheaper model
moments.mechanism: A cheaper model trained on 2.788 million H800 GPU hours briefly broke the belief that scale needs ever more Nvidia chips.
moments.outcome: NVIDIA lost over $589 billion of market value in a day, then recovered and passed $5 trillion in October.

moments.title: The hyperscalers' capex wall
moments.mechanism: Five hyperscalers are forecast to spend $803 to $828 billion in 2026, and NVIDIA's data-centre revenue equals about 45% of that capex.
moments.outcome: NVIDIA's revenue was $96.2 billion in the quarter to 26 July 2026, with $279 billion of purchase commitments.

periods.title: The American century
periods.what: One economy producing half of world output sets the monetary order, funds Europe and out-competes a planned rival.

periods.title: From transistor to integrated circuit
periods.what: Invention at a monopoly lab passes, through defection and patents, to venture-funded start-ups.

periods.title: The Fairchild diaspora
periods.what: Fairchild's alumni found dozens of firms, Intel among them.

periods.title: The microprocessor and the PC
periods.what: Intel moves from memory to the x86 as IBM-compatible PCs spread.

periods.title: Foundry and fabless
periods.what: TSMC builds for designers who own no fab; Nvidia is the clearest fabless winner.

periods.title: The GPU decade
periods.what: Gaming pays for a programmable parallel processor; CUDA makes it general.

periods.title: Deep learning on GPUs
periods.what: AlexNet proves that GPUs make deep learning practical; Nvidia's value rises from $7.66 billion to $117.26 billion.

periods.title: The scaling era
periods.what: The transformer is published, OpenAI scales it, Microsoft supplies the compute.

periods.title: The AI revolution
periods.what: ChatGPT, trillion-dollar chips, and a near-trillion-dollar valuation for each of two labs.
